prompt: `INTERNET` is declared in a manifest. When does the student grant it?

choices.text: Never: it is granted at install
choices.why: Right: normal permissions protect nothing private.

choices.text: In a dialog the first time the app goes online
choices.why: No dialog exists for normal permissions.

choices.text: On a special page in Settings
choices.why: That is for special permissions, like exact alarms.

choices.text: When the Play Store installs the update
choices.why: Install-time grants need no student action at all.

prompt: On Android 12, the student has refused the camera permission twice. The app calls the launcher again. What happens?
hint: From Android 11, two refusals are final.

choices.text: The permission is granted temporarily
choices.why: One-time grants exist, but only through the dialog.

choices.text: The dialog appears a third time
choices.why: After two refusals the system stops showing it.

choices.text: The launcher answers `false` at once, with no dialog
choices.why: Right: only Settings can change the answer now.

choices.text: The app crashes with a `SecurityException`
choices.why: Requesting is always allowed; the answer is simply no.

prompt: Why does the planner ask for `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` when the student taps "Turn on reminders" rather than when the app starts?
hint: A refusal costs one of two chances.

choices.text: The launcher cannot be created before the first screen
choices.why: It can be created in any composition.

choices.text: Robolectric cannot test a request at start-up
choices.why: Testability is not the reason; the student's trust is.

choices.text: Asking at start-up is forbidden by Android
choices.why: It is allowed, just unwise.

choices.text: The request then has context
choices.why: Right: a request with context is less likely to be refused, and a refusal is costly.

prompt: Which kind of permission is `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`?
hint: The student grants it in a dialog.

choices.text: Special
choices.why: Special ones are granted on a settings page.

choices.text: Runtime
choices.why: Right: since Android 13.

choices.text: Signature, reserved for system apps
choices.why: Any app may ask for it.

choices.text: Normal
choices.why: Normal ones are granted at install.

prompt: Why does `RemindersSetting` store a flag in `SharedPreferences` when the launcher answers?
hint: Android does not tell the app this.

choices.text: To remember that it has asked before
choices.why: Right: without it, never asked and refused twice look the same.

choices.text: Android requires apps to cache the permission's state
choices.why: It requires the opposite: check before use.

choices.text: To skip `checkSelfPermission` on later calls
choices.why: The function still checks every time; a cached grant can be revoked.

choices.text: So the dialog shows the student's previous answer
choices.why: The app cannot change the dialog.

prompt: After the launcher answers `false`, why does `RemindersSetting` ask Android about the rationale again instead of using that boolean alone?
hint: A refusal changes more than one thing.

choices.text: To show the dialog a second time automatically
choices.why: Asking again is the student's tap on the card.

choices.text: `false` might be a network error
choices.why: No network is involved in a permission request.

choices.text: A refusal also changes the advice
choices.why: Right: the boolean is the answer, not the whole state.

choices.text: The launcher's answer is unreliable on Android 13
choices.why: It is reliable; it just says less than the app needs.

prompt: Which call starts the permission request in section 03's code?

choices.text: `context.startActivity` with the permission's intent
choices.why: That call opens Settings, for the third card.

choices.text: `checkSelfPermission`
choices.why: It only reads the state.

choices.text: `launcher.launch(PERMISSION)`
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: `ActivityCompat.requestPermissions(activity, ...)` from the composable
choices.why: That older API exists, but this code uses the result launcher.

prompt: Compose's way to launch a permission dialog and receive the answer is `remember___ForActivityResult`.
On Android 15, the permission is not held, Android gives no advice to explain, and the app has never asked. What does `offerFor` return?

choices.text: `Explain`
choices.why: That needs the advice to be `true`.

choices.text: `OpenSettings`
choices.why: That needs `askedBefore`.

choices.text: `NotNeeded`
choices.why: That is below Android 13.

choices.text: `Ask`
choices.why: Right: never asked, so ask.

prompt: A colleague removes `askedBefore` from `offerFor`. Which student now gets the wrong card?
hint: Two states look identical to Android.

choices.text: One who granted it
choices.why: The `granted` branch is unaffected.

choices.text: One who refused twice
choices.why: Right: without the app's memory, refused twice looks like never asked.

choices.text: One on Android 12
choices.why: The `sdk` branch still handles it first.

choices.text: One who refused once
choices.why: Android's advice is `true` there, so `Explain` still appears.

prompt: Why is `offerFor` tested with plain JUnit rather than Robolectric?

choices.text: JUnit tests are required for every `when`
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: Robolectric would grant the permission automatically
choices.why: It does not; and the function never asks it.

choices.text: Robolectric cannot run enum classes
choices.why: It runs any Kotlin.

choices.text: It takes plain values and touches no Android API
choices.why: Right: the Android calls stay in the composable, and the decision is a table.

prompt: How many rows of the printed table, below the header, came out as `NotNeeded`?
Why is the third card's button outlined rather than filled?
hint: Where does it take the student?

choices.text: It leaves the app
choices.why: Right: section 05 says so.

choices.text: Filled buttons are not allowed in a `Card`
choices.why: The first two cards have filled ones.

choices.text: Outlined buttons cannot be clicked twice
choices.why: They behave like any button.

choices.text: Material 3 requires outlined buttons after a refusal
choices.why: No such rule; it is a design choice.

prompt: `ReminderCard` takes an `Offer` and two lambdas. What does that make easy?

choices.text: Showing the system dialog inside the card

choices.text: Granting the permission in tests
choices.why: The card knows nothing about permissions.

choices.text: Drawing each state on its own
choices.why: Right: the screenshot test passes each `Offer` directly.

choices.text: Skipping recomposition
choices.why: Recomposition is unaffected.

prompt: Which explanation would section 05 accept for the second card?

choices.text: "Most apps need this permission"

choices.text: "One reminder a day at most, nothing else"
choices.why: Right: specific, true and checkable.

choices.text: "Allow notifications to get the most out of the planner"
choices.why: It says nothing a student can weigh.

choices.text: "Notifications are required to continue"
choices.why: It is false, and a threat.

prompt: An app granted the camera "only this time" yesterday. Today it opens the camera without checking. What does section 07 imply?

choices.text: The grant still holds until the next reboot
choices.why: A one-time grant ends soon after the app leaves the screen.

choices.text: Android upgrades it to a permanent grant
choices.why: Only the student can grant permanently.

prompt: Put yourself on Android 15: the planner has asked once and been refused, and Android advises an explanation. Which card shows, and what does its button do?

choices.text: "Reminders are on"

choices.text: The settings card; the button opens Settings

choices.text: `Explain`, and a second request
